text.p: Following are some of the main stories in Dutch newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
FINANCIEELE DAGBLAD
- Dutch central bank DNB increases its special advance rate to 2.7 pct from 2.5 pct. (p1)
- ABN Amro bank says current bourse climate should prompt extra caution. (p1)
- Dutch economic growth outstrips rest of Europe and U.S. (p1)
- Chemical concern Akzo Nobel posts flat 1996 earnings. (p1)
- Building concern Ballast-Nedam estimates five percent profits growth in 1997. (p3)
- German activities push construction company BAM into the red. (p3)
- Retailer Macintosh is expecting clearly better net results in the current year. (p1)
- Government's planned sale of information technology group Roccade is short-sighted, says director of consultants Berenschots. (p7) -
VOLKSKRANT
- The Christian Democrats (CDA) would drop dramatically from their current 34 parliamentary seats to a historical low of 26 if elections were held today, according to a poll. (p1)
- Parliamentarians throw away three quarters of memorandums unread, according to research. (p1)
- Accord between Royal Dutch Airlines/KLM and its U.S. partner Northwest Airlines might lead to KLM selling its minority stake in NWA. (p2)
- Dutch citizens and businesses profited on a large scale from the deportation of jews during World War Two, says Professor Lipschits. (p3)
DE TELEGRAAF
- The Netherlands is popular with foreign investors. (p1)
- Murderer of foreign affairs minister Hans van Mierlo's mother-in-law arrested in Huddersfield, England. (p1)
- Copyright organisation Buma/Stemra estimates Dutch market for bootleg CD's at one hundred million guilders. (p6)
- Steel maker Hoogovens reaches agreement on taking a 50 pct stake in Belgium's steel concern Boel. (p23)
ALGEMEEN DAGBLAD
- Malaysian government and investors ask for clarification regarding Dutch cabinet's plans for relaunching bankrupt aircraft maker Fokker. (p1)
- Van Ommeren aims to become the world's largest tank storage concern. (p12)
TROUW
- Vice premier Hans Dijkstal does not expect his Liberal Party's differing standpoint, concerning NATO expansion to be a cause for a crisis. (p1)
